bull_bear.body: - Holding-company support structure: the Company has no employees and its Key Managerial Personnel are deputed by Lodha Developers Limited, and it relies on group-level frameworks - the Lodha cyber-security incident report process and the group anti-money-laundering / anti-bribery / anti-corruption policy hosted on the holding company's website.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- No operating business and no pipeline - the Company is effectively dormant — The Board's Report states: 'The Company's real estate project was completed in 2018. The Company does not have any ongoing business operations and does not intend to undertake any new real estate development project. The Company trades in building and construction materials.' The MD&A repeats twice that the Company 'does not have any project and has no plan to take up any real estate project in near future'. Everything the MD&A says about housing demand therefore describes an industry the Company no longer participates in.
- Total customer / counterparty concentration on the holding company — BRSR Principle 1 Essential Indicator 9 ('Open-ness of business') discloses Share of RPTs - Sales to related parties as a percentage of total sales at 100% in FY 2026 versus 40% in FY 2025, with sales to dealers/distributors NIL and no trading houses used. Loans and advances given to related parties were 100% of total loans and advances in FY 2025 and NIL in FY 2026. The revenue base is thus a single related counterparty.
- Complete dependence on the holding company for management capacity — 'The Company does not have any employee. The KMPs are deputed by the holding company.' The BRSR adds that the Company has no employees or workers, that directors draw no remuneration from the Company, and that governance frameworks (anti-bribery policy, cyber-security incident process) sit at Lodha group level. The Company has no independent operating organisation.
- Pending merger by absorption into Lodha Developers Limited - the listed entity may cease to exist — The Board's Report discloses that an application for a Scheme of Merger by Absorption with holding company Lodha Developers Limited was filed before the NCLT, Mumbai Bench on June 11, 2026 under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013. No timeline, swap ratio or approval status is stated in the supplied text; the report points to the notes to the financial statements for further detail.
- Sector labour intensity and input-cost / land-price inflation — MD&A Risks and Concerns: 'The real estate sector is heavily dependent on manpower. There is a need for development of technologically less labour-intensive alternative methods of construction. Further, the increase in land prices, inputs costs are risks to the industry.'
- Interest-cost and liquidity risk to demand and margins — MD&A: 'Higher interest cost would dent margins and may have a direct effect on the customer's cash flow as well. Increase in end product prices coupled with tight liquidity may impact demand.'
- Tax and levy burden compressing margins — MD&A: 'The various taxes and levies would add to the costs and this is likely to squeeze margins as end product prices may not go up correspondingly.' The cautionary statement further names changes in government regulations and tax regimes, material availability and prices, and cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's principal markets as factors that could make actual results differ materially.
- Unresolved disputed tax and legal claims (back-filled with provenance) — BACK-FILLED from the notes to the financial statements, which appear in the profile and governance_entities sibling bundles and not in this one: contingent liabilities are disclosed as 'Claims against the Company not acknowledged as debts' in two buckets - Disputed Taxation Matters and Disputed Other Legal Cases (amounts deliberately not reproduced). The note states the contingent liabilities exclude the undeterminable outcome of pending litigations, and that the Company has assessed that an outflow of resources embodying economic benefits is not probable.
- Governance concentration - a peak-cycle warning management itself records — MD&A Opportunities: 'Because housing has been in a secular uptrend over the last 4-5 years, there are concerns of this being the peak of the cycle and demand softening going forward.' Management states its own belief that India is 'only in the early stages of a multi decade housing upcycle', so the downside case is acknowledged but not adopted.

outlook.body:
- Take up no new real estate projects - the MD&A states twice, verbatim, 'The Company does not have any project and has no plan to take up any real estate project in near future', and the Board's Report adds that the Company 'does not intend to undertake any new real estate development project'.
- Run the Company as a trading entity: its real estate project was completed in 2018, it has no ongoing business operations, and it trades in building and construction materials.
- Consolidate into the parent - an application for a Scheme of Merger by Absorption with holding company Lodha Developers Limited was filed before the NCLT, Mumbai Bench on June 11, 2026 under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Operate with zero employees: 'The Company does not have any employee. The KMPs are deputed by the holding company.'
- Retain earnings for FY 2025-26 - no dividend recommended and no transfer to reserves, within a Board-adopted Dividend Distribution Policy framed under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations.
- Retention over distribution for the year under review: the Board did not recommend any dividend for FY 2025-26 and proposed no transfer to reserves. The framework is a Board-formulated and adopted Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations, which sets out the parameters and circumstances the Board considers in deciding between distributing dividend to shareholders and retaining profits; it is published in the investor section of www.nsil.net.in. There was no change in the authorised or paid-up share capital during FY 2025-26. Reinvestment intent is explicitly negative: the Company's real estate project was completed in 2018, it has no ongoing business operations, states it does not intend to undertake any new real estate development project and has no plan to take up any real estate project in the near future; it trades in building and construction materials. The structural end-state proposed is absorption into the holding company - an application for a Scheme of Merger by Absorption with Lodha Developers Limited was filed before the NCLT, Mumbai Bench on June 11, 2026. Directors draw no remuneration from the Company and hold no shares in it; KMPs are on deputation from the holding company.
- NO ESG TARGETS SET - a stated absence, not silence: BRSR Section B item 5, 'Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the entity with defined timelines, if any', is answered 'N.A. [Refer note in Section I (13)]', and item 6 (performance against such commitments) is likewise 'N A.'
- No specified Committee of the Board or Director is responsible for decision-making on sustainability-related issues (BRSR Section B item 9: 'No'); no statement by a director responsible for the BR report highlighting ESG challenges and targets (item 7: 'N.A.').
- No independent external assessment or evaluation of the working of the policies (BRSR Section B item 11: 'No'); no BRSR assurance - both 'Name of assurance provider' and 'Type of assurance obtained' are 'NA'.
- Policies are stated to cover all nine NGRBC principles (P1-P9 all 'Yes') and to have been translated into procedures (all 'Yes'), with web link www.nsil.net.in; Board approval was obtained 'wherever necessary'. Review of performance against policies and of statutory compliance is done annually by the CEO in the Board Meeting; the Board of Directors supported by the CEO are the highest authority for implementation.
- All Principle 6 environmental indicators are answered 'N.A.' - energy consumption and intensity, PAT-scheme designated consumer status, water withdrawal and discharge, Zero Liquid Discharge, air emissions, Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions and intensity, GHG-reduction projects, waste management, ecologically sensitive area operations and environmental impact assessments. The single substantive environmental answer is: 'The entity is compliant with the stated laws' (Water Act, Air Act, Environment Protection Act and rules).
- No codes, certifications, labels or standards (FSC, Fairtrade, Rainforest Alliance, Trustea, SA 8000, OHSAS, ISO, BIS) are mapped to any principle - BRSR Section B item 4 is answered 'N.A.'
- Cyber-security and data privacy: a framework/policy is in place, supported by IT policies on software usage, password management and information security plus the Lodha group cyber-security incident report process, published at https://www.lodhagroup.in/sustainability/. Data breaches in FY 2026: Nil, with nil involving personally identifiable information and no impact.
- Ethics and compliance: Nil fines/penalties/punishment/award/compounding fees/settlement amounts in proceedings with regulators, law-enforcement agencies or judicial institutions; no disciplinary action for bribery or corruption against any director or KMP; no conflict-of-interest complaints. The anti-money-laundering, anti-bribery and anti-corruption policy is hosted on the HOLDING COMPANY's website, not the Company's own.
- Board and KMP training coverage: 6 training and awareness programmes for the Board of Directors and 3 for Key Managerial Personnel, covering all 9 principles, with 100% of persons in each category covered. Employees and workers: 'N.A.' - the Company has none.
- Complaints: 1 shareholder complaint filed in FY 2026 and 1 in FY 2025, with Nil pending resolution at the close of each year; Nil customer complaints across data privacy, advertising, cyber-security, delivery of essential services, restrictive trade practices, unfair trade practices and other in both FY 2026 and FY 2025; Nil product recalls. Grievance redressal mechanisms exist for Shareholders and Customers at http://nsil.net.in/investor-relation/policies.
- Nil affiliations with trade and industry chambers or associations, and no corrective action on anti-competitive conduct ('N.A.').
- Only one stakeholder group is identified as key - Shareholders (not vulnerable/marginalised), engaged quarterly and annually through the annual report and quarterly financial results, to 'provide updated information about the Company'.
- The BRSR 'material responsible business conduct issues' table (Section A item 26) - normally the richest source of company-identified ESG risks and mitigations - is answered 'N.A. Refer note in Section I (13)', so no materiality assessment is disclosed.
- Reporting boundary is standalone and covers only National Standard (India) Limited; because it has no employees or workers it reports only on Essential and Leadership Indicators to the extent applicable, and directs readers to Lodha Developers Limited's consolidated BRSR for FY 2025-26 on www.lodhagroup.com and both stock exchanges for group-level ESG performance.

outlook.body:
- CONTEXT FLAG: the MD&A demand narrative below is about the Indian real estate INDUSTRY, not the Company's own revenue - the same MD&A states 'The Company does not have any project and has no plan to take up any real estate project in near future.'
- Management believes India is 'only in the early stages of a multi decade housing upcycle', with a large and growing population, strong economy, high single-digit wage growth and urbanisation expected to drive housing demand.
- Structural demand drivers and industry dynamics are expected to generate significant housing demand and to translate into 'robust pre-sales in the years ahead'.
- Anticipated interest-rate reductions and government-led tax rebates are expected to provide additional impetus to the affordable and mid-income housing segments.
- A visible shift in customer preference towards branded developers, recognising the importance of execution capability; residential markets across top Indian cities are entering a phase of greater maturity with more measured growth, increased competition among branded developers and a focus on timely execution, quality and affordability.
- Macro backdrop stated: the Indian economy is projected to grow by 6.6% in FY27 versus 7.7% in FY26 (RBI also expects around 6.6% in FY27), with the slowdown attributed to higher crude prices in the aftermath of the Iran-USA war; retail inflation has hardened to 3.9% in May-26 versus 2.8% in May-25.
- Management flags the counter-case it does not endorse: 'there are concerns of this being the peak of the cycle and demand softening going forward', which it counters with India's need for quality housing and low home-ownership capability levels.

meta.thesis: National Standard (India) Limited is a 1962-incorporated, BSE-listed Lodha group company whose only real estate project was completed in 2018 and which now derives its revenue from trading in building and construction materials, pending a proposed merger by absorption into its holding company Lodha Developers Limited.
